title: UPLB Sweet mangosteen (NSIC Mt 01): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: UPLB Sweet mangosteen: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: UPLB Sweet mangosteen is a mangosteen variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: UPLB Sweet is a registered mangosteen variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mt 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2005 as NSIC 2005 Mt 01. Dept. of Horti UPLB c/o Leon Namuco bred it. Its record notes a yield of 1,148 fruits.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Mt 01, this is the same mangosteen. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [mangosteen variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about UPLB Sweet mangosteen

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of UPLB Sweet was about 55 years old and about 4 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 1,148 fruits. It bears every other year, with fruit in July August. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit mangosteen fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of UPLB Sweet weighs about 87 grams, and its shape is ovate. The flesh is snowy white and smooth. Its sweetness measured 18.65 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 29 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as July August, bearing biennial.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits July to August, bears every other year, mangosteen trees may take 6 to 12 or more years to first fruit.
**Yield:** About 1,148 fruits on the mother tree.
**Fruit:** About 87 g, purple rind, snowy white, juicy flesh, about 18.7 Brix, usually 1 seed.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the first registered mangosteen, from a 55 year old UPLB tree that bore over 1,100 fruits. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant UPLB Sweet mangosteen

Mangosteen is slow, often seven years or more to bear. Plant in deep, moist soil with some shade while young. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Mt 01 the same as UPLB Sweet?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mt 01 is another name for UPLB Sweet, registered as NSIC 2005 Mt 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 1,148 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of UPLB Sweet?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
